title: Renewal health ops quick reference - latency, cost, uptime, cache
content:
Purpose:
This quick reference is a lightweight QBR-ready primer for CS managers and SEs preparing renewal conversations. Focused on the four signals we repeatedly see move renewal risk: latency (tail and median), uptime (availability), cost-per-token economics, and cache hit rate.

What this doc is (and is not):
- Not a deep SRE runbook — links to runbooks are in linked_artifacts.
- Not final policy — a compact checklist and definitions page designed for QBR decks and renewal readiness checks.
- Includes monitoring snippets, suggested targets, and immediate playbook actions for green/yellow/red states.

Summary definitions (plain language):
1) Latency (P50, P95, P99)
- What: Time from request enter -> first-byte for streaming or final token latency for non-streaming generation.
- Why it matters: User-perceived responsiveness (P50) and worst-case experience (P95/P99). Tail latency is the leading driver of product churn for interactive features.
- Measurement note: Report both a) user-facing API latency (client->Redwood edge) and b) server-side inference latency (edge excluded). Use request tagging to separate embedding vs. completion workloads.
- Example metric names: api.latency.ms{route=chat,region=us-east}.p95, runtime.infer.ms{model=redwood-3b}.p99.

2) Uptime / Availability (SLA/SLO)
- What: Percentage of successful requests over total attempts (success = 2xx + expected streaming partials; failures = 4xx/5xx/timeouts/connection errors).
- Window: 30d rolling is the default for renewal dashboards; include 7d for recency signals.
- Measurement: Exclude maintenance windows, but include autoscaling-related errors. For Dedicated/private customers, also show infra-level events (node reboots, network incidents).
- Example: availability.30d.percent{customer=ACME} = 99.92%

3) Cost per served token (effective unit cost)
- What: Billable cost (vendor + Redwood compute attribution) divided by served tokens in the window. We use two flavors: gross cost/token (what the customer bill shows) and effective cost/token after cache savings.
- Calculation notes: Include model-specific GPU minutes, batching efficiency, and cache hit savings. For multi-model fallbacks, normalize to tokens served by primary model equivalent.
- Example: cost_per_1k_tokens.usd{model=stable-7b} = (gpu_cost + infra + licensing) / (tokens_served / 1000).

4) Cache hit rate (prefix + KV)
- What: Fraction of requests (or tokens) served from cache vs full inference. We break this into:
  a) prefix cache hit rate (re-requests identical prompt prefix)
  b) KV cache reuse (within-session KV reuse for long chats)
- Why: High cache hit = lower effective cost, lower latency, and fewer tail spikes.
- Measurement caveat: Warmup bias — newly onboarded customers will have low hit rates until cache is populated. Report both raw hit and hit after 14d warmup.

KPI table (compact, QBR-friendly)
- Table columns: Metric | Definition | Suggested renewal-tier target | Check cadence | Owner | Quick runbook action if off-target
- Sample rows (paste into slide):
  * Latency P50 | median end-to-end API latency for primary chat route | < 150 ms | daily | CS + SRE | Check burst autoscaler, model variant routing, enable KV cache for session traffic
  * Latency P95 | 95th percentile API latency | < 450 ms | daily | CS + SRE | Identify long-tail model invocations, throttle large-seq requests, suggest quantized model variant or batching config
  * Availability 30d | % of successful requests (no infra maintenance) | >= 99.9% | 30d rolling | CS + SRE | Verify incident log, enable fallback model region, increase dedicated capacity if sustained errors
  * Effective cost / 1k tokens | USD per 1k served tokens (post-cache) | <= $0.40 (SMB) / <= $0.18 (enterprise committed) | weekly | CS + Finops | Propose batching/quantization/commit plan; run Optimize recommendations
  * Cache hit rate (14d adjusted) | % of eligible requests served from cache | >= 55% | weekly | CS + Solutions Eng | Add explicit prefix hashing, advise prompt templates, enable persistent session caching

Technical query examples (to hand to SRE/infra):
- P95 latency (api): sum(rate(request_duration_ms_bucket{le="500",route="/chat",customer="{{cust}}"}[5m])) / sum(rate(requests_total{route="/chat",customer="{{cust}}"}[5m]))
- Cache hit rate: increase(cache_hits_total{customer="{{cust}}"}[30d]) / increase(cache_lookup_total{customer="{{cust}}"}[30d])
- Cost per token: increase(billing_cost_usd_total{customer="{{cust}}"}[30d]) / (increase(tokens_served_total{customer="{{cust}}"}[30d]) / 1000)

Renewal impact matrix (simple):
- Green: All metrics within target or improving. Talk: upsell + committed/Dedicated conversation.
- Yellow: One signal slightly off-target (e.g., P95 high or cache low). Talk: mitigation plan, short-term SLA commitments, Optimize run.
- Red: Multiple signals off-target or >3 incidents in 30d. Talk: immediate remediation, potential credit, escalate to Solutions Eng + SRE weekly warroom.

Playbook actions (checklist style):
1) First pass (CS owner): collect 30/7 day numbers, console screenshots, and last 3 incident tickets.
2) Quick mitigation (within 48 hrs): enable fallback model routing, reduce max_sequence_token on heavy routes, and set short-lived rate limits for bursty clients.
3) Mid-term (2–14 days): enable KV cache for chat sessions, enable prefix cache where safe, run Redwood Optimize suggestions for batching or quantization.
4) Long-term (30+ days): propose reserved capacity commit or dedicated pool if predictable high volume.

Common Qs & notes to self:
- Q: Should we include client-side retries in availability calc? A: No — measure server-side availability only. Track client retries as separate telemetry.
- Q: How to surface model fallback cost effect? A: Show blended effective cost per token with and without fallbacks for the renewal window.
- TODO: add sample deck slide images (screenshot placeholders) and a one-page handout for customers describing "What we measure and why".

Slide-ready checklist for QBR prep (24–72 hours before meeting):
- Pull 30d and 7d dashboards for the four signals (attach PNGs).
- Prepare one incident timeline for any availability/latency incidents.
- Run Optimize recommendations and capture the top 2 cost-saving levers.
- Map current metrics to renewal cadence: show delta vs previous quarter and recommended action.
- Draft a short ask (commit level, trial dedicated, or SE engagement) and recommended timeline.

Appendix: Example customer snapshot (fictional)
- Window: 30d ending 2026-02-15
- P50 latency: 122 ms | P95: 410 ms | Availability: 99.84% | Cost/1k tokens: $0.62 gross / $0.28 effective | Cache hit (14d adj): 39%
- Recommended immediate actions: enable session KV cache, open SE ticket for prompt template refactor, propose 6-month reserved capacity trial.

- SE backup: Jonah Castillo (jonah@redwood.ai)

Notes: keep this doc short in the QBR slide deck; drive the conversation with two numbers (trend + root cause for any red/yellow signals).

End of doc.
